title: New biomarkers in patients with acute and chronic heart failure
summary:
After giving consent, participants receive detailed written and verbal information about the study. The study begins with an initial examination in the emergency department (Day 0), including a standard blood test and a 12-lead ECG.
On Days 3 and 5, further blood samples are taken – including additional tubes for biomarker analysis – and two short questionnaires are completed (PHQ-9 and KCCQ-12) to assess mental health and quality of life. On the day of hospital discharge, a final check-up is performed, including another ECG and an echocardiogram to monitor any changes during the hospital stay.
After discharge, follow-up appointments take place at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. These outpatient visits include blood tests (including biomarkers), an ECG, echocardiography, a 6-minute walking test to assess physical capacity, and the same questionnaires.
Participants can leave the study at any time, for example, if they withdraw consent or for medical reasons. The study does not include testing for infectious diseases (HIV, hepatitis) or substance use.
Study goal:
The aim is to investigate whether specific biomarkers in the blood (Semaphorins and BMPs) are linked to the severity of heart failure. The results will support the development of improved diagnostic and treatment strategies.
conditions: compensated heart failure, stable heart failure

interventions.name: Patients who were hospitalized at the University Medical Center Mannheim (UMM) due to acute decompensation of their heart failure
Patients in a recompensated state of their heart failure who have regular appointments at the heart failure outpatient clinic at UMM

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who meet the criteria for the diagnosis of chronic heart failure, provide informed consent to participate in the study, and demonstrate willingness to attend follow-up visits at the heart failure outpatient clinic.
Exclusion criteria:
-Patients unable to provide informed consent or under legal guardianship
-Patients under 18 years of age
-Pregnant women
-Advanced malignant disease
-Liver cirrhosis, Child C
-Patients requiring dialysis
